definitions.gloss: lining up; standing in a row; forming an orderly line
definitions.explanation: Arranging people or things in a neat, orderly row or formation. Commonly used in school, military, and public contexts.

examples.japanese: {生徒|せいと}たちが{校庭|こうてい}に{整列|せいれつ}した。
examples.english: The students lined up in the schoolyard.

examples.japanese: 「{整列|せいれつ}！」と{先生|せんせい}が{号令|ごうれい}をかけた。
ホームで{電車|でんしゃ}を{待|ま}つ{乗客|じょうきゃく}がきちんと{整列|せいれつ}している{光景|こうけい}は、{海外|かいがい}からの{旅行者|りょこうしゃ}を{驚|おどろ}かせる。
examples.english: The sight of passengers lining up neatly on the platform to wait for the train surprises travelers from overseas.

notes:
USAGE:
{整列|せいれつ} is used with する as an intransitive suru-verb. People line up (に{整列|せいれつ}する) at or in a location.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一列|いちれつ}に{整列|せいれつ}する (to line up in a single row)
- きちんと{整列|せいれつ}する (to line up neatly)
- {整列|せいれつ}の{号令|ごうれい} (command to line up)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {整列|せいれつ}: lining up in orderly formation (formal, organized)
- {並|なら}ぶ: to line up, to stand in a row (everyday, general)
- {行列|ぎょうれつ}: a queue, a line of people (the resulting line itself)
